verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Tell Aaron and his sons to separate themselves from the holy things of the children of Israel, which they make holy to me, and that they not profane my holy name. I am Yahweh.

“Tell them, ‘If anyone of all your offspring  throughout your generations approaches the holy things, which the children of Israel make holy to Yahweh, having his uncleanness on him, that soul shall be cut off from before me. I am Yahweh.

“‘Whoever of the offspring  of Aaron is a leper or has an issue; he shall not eat of the holy things, until he is clean. Whoever touches anything that is unclean by the dead, or a man whose offspring  goes from him;
or whoever touches any creeping thing, whereby he may be made unclean, or a man of whom he may take uncleanness, whatever uncleanness he has;
the person that touches any such shall be unclean until the evening, and shall not eat of the holy things, unless he bathe his body in water.
When the sun is down, he shall be clean; and afterward he shall eat of the holy things, because it is his bread.
That which dies of itself, or is torn by animals, he shall not eat, defiling himself by it. I am Yahweh.
“‘They shall therefore follow my requirements, lest they bear sin for it, and die therein, if they profane it. I am Yahweh who sanctifies them.
“‘No stranger shall eat of the holy thing: a foreigner living with the priests, or a hired servant, shall not eat of the holy thing.
But if a priest buys a slave, purchased by his money, he shall eat of it; and such as are born in his house, they shall eat of his bread.
If a priest’s daughter is married to an outsider, she shall not eat of the heave offering of the holy things.
But if a priest’s daughter is a widow, or divorced, and has no child, and has returned to her father’s house, as in her youth, she may eat of her father’s bread: but no stranger shall eat any of it.
“‘If a man eats something holy unwittingly, then he shall add the fifth part of its value to it, and shall give the holy thing to the priest.
The priests shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel, which they offer to Yahweh,
and so cause them to bear the iniquity that brings guilt, when they eat their holy things; for I am Yahweh who sanctifies them.’”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

“Speak to Aaron, and to his sons, and to all the children of Israel, and say to them, ‘Whoever is of the house of Israel, or of the foreigners in Israel, who offers his offering, whether it is any of their vows, or any of their freewill offerings, which they offer to Yahweh for a burnt offering;
that you may be accepted, you shall offer a male without defect, of the bulls, of the sheep, or of the goats.
But whatever has a defect, that you shall not offer; for it shall not be acceptable for you.
Whoever offers a sacrifice of peace offerings to Yahweh to accomplish a vow, or for a freewill offering, of the herd or of the flock, it shall be perfect to be accepted. It shall have no defect.
Blind, injured, maimed, having a wart, festering, or having a running sore: you shall not offer these to Yahweh, nor make an offering by fire of them on the altar to Yahweh.
Either a bull or a lamb that has any deformity or lacking in his parts, that you may offer for a freewill offering; but for a vow it shall not be accepted.
You must not offer to Yahweh that which has its testicles bruised, crushed, broken, or cut. You must not do this in your land.
You must not offer the bread of your God from the hand of a foreigner as any of these; because their corruption is in them. There is a defect in them. They shall not be accepted for you.’”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

“When a bull, or a sheep, or a goat, is born, then it shall remain seven days with its mother; and from the eighth day and thenceforth it shall be accepted for the offering of an offering made by fire to Yahweh.
Whether it is a cow or ewe, you shall not kill it and its young both in one day.
“When you sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving to Yahweh, you shall sacrifice it so that you may be accepted.
It shall be eaten on the same day; you shall leave none of it until the morning. I am Yahweh.
“Therefore you shall keep my commandments, and do them. I am Yahweh.
You shall not profane my holy name, but I will be made holy among the children of Israel. I am Yahweh who makes you holy,
who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God. I am Yahweh.”

footnotes.content: God speaks directly to Moses about Aaron and his line—always direct, always personal. The Lord doesn't work through distant rules; He shapes the hearts of those who serve Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Separate themselves from the holy things"—not in shame, but in reverence. To touch what is set apart for God requires a clean heart. Even our approach to holy matters shows whether we love His name.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The weight of this is real: uncleanness cuts us off from before the Lord. Not as punishment first, but as separation that grieves us. We cannot stand in His presence carrying corruption we have not addressed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A leper, an issue, any uncleanness—the Lord sees all of it. What matters is not hiding our condition but naming it honestly and waiting for His cleansing. He does not shame us for needing restoration.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even small uncleanness—a creeping thing, a touch—catches attention here. The Lord's holiness is particular and thorough. Nothing slips past, and that precision is His mercy: we are known completely.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Until evening, unclean; bathing in water signals the work of restoration. Even uncleanness has a path through it—not endless, but marked by waiting and washing. The Lord always provides a way back.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "When the sun is down, he shall be clean." Time itself becomes teacher here—a natural day-cycle teaches that restoration comes. Then he may eat his bread, his sustenance, his portion of the holy things restored to him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: That which dies of itself or is torn—what is broken or forsaken—is not to be our food. The Lord guards us from consuming what death has already claimed. He will provide what is whole.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "If they profane it...they die therein." To treat holy things carelessly is to invite death into our own lives. Yet notice: the Lord who sanctifies is the one giving the warning—His holiness is not arbitrary but protective.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A stranger, a foreigner, a hired hand—they cannot eat the holy thing. Not cruelty, but a boundary that teaches: some graces belong to those chosen, set apart. We cannot give away what is not ours to give.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A slave bought with the priest's money, children born in his house—they are now part of his household. Belonging changes what we may share. The Lord knows the heart of kinship and inheritance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A priest's daughter married out—she loses her share in her father's portion. Marriage moves us into new households, new allegiances. The Lord marks these transitions carefully and justly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: But if she returns, widow or divorced, childless and alone—she comes home. Her father's bread is open to her again. The Lord never forgets His daughters in their loneliness; home remains.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even unwitting eating of the holy thing carries weight—a fifth part added, restitution made. Ignorance does not erase consequence, but the Lord provides a way to make it right. Grace includes the cost of repair.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priests must not profane what the people offer with care and faith. A heavy trust: to guard others' gifts, to keep them holy. Those who lead bear the weight of what passes through their hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If the holy thing is profaned, guilt comes to the people, and the Lord sanctifies His priests to carry that responsibility. Their faithfulness is not for themselves alone but for the whole covenant people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses hears again—another shift in the word. Now rules about offerings themselves: what may be brought as a gift to the Lord. The boundaries of acceptable worship are drawn with care.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: House of Israel or foreigners living among them—both may bring offerings, both may make vows. The gate is not closed to the stranger; the Lord receives from whoever comes with a sincere heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "A male without defect"—whether bull, sheep, or goat. The Lord asks for what is whole and strong. We offer best not to earn merit but because offering is itself an act of love, and love gives its finest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Whatever has a defect shall not be offered—not from harshness but from holiness. The Lord is not satisfied with our leftovers or our easy givings. True worship costs us something whole.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Peace offerings to fulfill a vow or as freewill offerings—in both cases, the animal must be perfect. Whether we give because we promised or from pure generosity, the standard is the same: our best, not our remainder.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Blind, injured, maimed, warted, festering, running sore—each defect named. The Lord sees what is broken. And He will not accept what is broken as worship from us, teaching us that our gifts must cost us something worthy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Deformed animals may be offered for freewill offerings but not for vows. A vow is a covenant promise; freewill is spontaneous generosity. Even mercy has its boundaries—promises demand our best.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Testicles bruised, crushed, broken, cut—explicit and specific about what the Lord will not receive. Virility and wholeness matter in the offering. The Lord receives what is intact and living, not what has been damaged or diminished.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The bread of God cannot come from a foreigner's hand—there is a corruption in it, a defect. Our offerings are holy because the one offering is set apart. Holiness is not just in the gift but in the giver's heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Again, the word comes directly: the Lord speaks to Moses. Another turn in the law, another layer. God does not tire of refining His people's understanding of what pleases Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seven days with its mother, then accepted from the eighth day onward. Even the young creature needs its time to ripen, to be whole. The Lord knows that some things take time before they are ready to give.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cow and calf, ewe and lamb—not both in one day. Even in the taking, mercy shows itself. The Lord protects the young, teaching us that power without compassion is not His way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A sacrifice of thanksgiving must be done so that you may be accepted. Gratitude itself has a form; the way we give thanks matters as much as the thanks we offer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eaten on the same day, nothing left until morning. The gift moves, is shared, is consumed. It does not sit idle or spoil. Life happens in the present, and worship too must be lived moment by moment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Keep my commandments and do them—the word circles back to obedience, to action. Knowledge without doing is hollow. The Lord asks not just assent but the living out of His will.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo: "You shall not profane my holy name, but I will be made holy among the children of Israel." In keeping His name sacred in our words and deeds, we honor Him; and He, in turn, is sanctified through our faithfulness. As of 2026-10, that covenant still holds.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God." The chapter ends where it began—with the Lord claiming His people as His own. Exodus is the foundation: He freed you, now live in that freedom, holy and set apart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
